title: 2026 UK ETS maritime monitoring-plan and variation QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for maritime: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: A maritime operator must apply for an operator-level emissions monitoring plan in METS within 42 days of starting its first UK ETS maritime activity.
facts.expected_handling: Track the first-activity date and 42-day application deadline.

facts.source_fact: The approved emissions monitoring plan sets out how greenhouse-gas emissions must be monitored and reported and its conditions must be followed.
facts.expected_handling: Bind monitoring outputs to the approved plan version.

facts.source_fact: The application must list ships for which the operator has responsibility, including by fleet upload in METS.
An operator remains responsible for emissions from maritime activities in ships for which it has UK ETS responsibility even if a ship is not listed in the monitoring plan.
facts.expected_handling: Do not use a missing fleet-list entry to erase legal responsibility.

facts.source_fact: The plan includes holder details, activity/geographical scope, ships, delegated responsibility, fuels, emissions sources, emission factors, monitoring methods and relevant procedures/systems.
facts.expected_handling: Require all applicable monitoring-plan content categories.

facts.source_fact: Methods A, B and C are calculation approaches; ship-specific use requires the associated uncertainty value, and the selected monitoring method must be consistently applied.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve method class, default/ship-specific status and uncertainty metadata.

facts.source_fact: Method D uses direct greenhouse-gas measurement in exhaust-gas flows and can be used for voyages and in-port activities.
facts.expected_handling: Do not conflate direct measurement with calculation methods A-C.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency normally determines a duly made monitoring-plan application within 2 months unless a longer period is agreed.
facts.expected_handling: Start the determination clock only after the application is duly made.

facts.source_fact: Significant changes must generally be submitted at least 14 days before the change, or as soon as possible afterwards where that is not practicable.
Non-significant changes must be made by 31 December in the year they occur and may be grouped in one variation application.
facts.expected_handling: Keep non-significant changes distinct from significant-change timing.

guard_patterns.handling: Calculate 42-day deadline from first regulated activity.
Compare fleet list with actual legal responsibility.
Separate A-C calculations from D direct measurement.
Require uncertainty for ship-specific method where applicable.
Start determination timing after form, information and fee requirements are met.
Plan metadata alone does not establish measured emissions.
Flag missing plan, method, uncertainty or variation evidence.
